(By Pleader Shri Afzal  Ahmed)
 SCCH-18 2 MVC 6098/2024  JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That, on 22.07.2024 at about 10.10 a.m. the petitioner was riding the Scooter bearing No. KA-04- Shaik Rafiulla G vs B.M.T.C on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74538220/
1 HZ-8076, near Krishan Vihar gate, Jayamahal Main Road, JC Nagara, Bengaluru, at that time,
driver of the BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2151 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous head injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital wherein he took treatment as an inpatient, undergone surgery and had spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4.

It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 59 years and working as a Head Master at Quwathula Islam High School, Bengaluru and getting an income of Rs.1,33,638/- per month.
After the accident, he could not able to do any work as earlier.
5. It is stated that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2151.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional R.T. Nagar Police in Crime No.63/2024.
As such, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking compensation.
6. In response to the notice, the respondent has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
7. In the written statement, the respondent contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.
Further the respondent has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner and expenses incurred towards medication and other incidental charges.

The respondent stated that on the date of the accident the bus in question was on its Schedule route from Peenya 2nd Stage to Shivajinagar, on 22.01.2024 while the said bus was proceeding on the schedule route from Peenya 2nd Stage to Shivajinagar driven by its driver slowly and cautiously observing all the traffic rules and regulations at about 10.15 a.m. the driver of the bus stopped the bus at Mekri circle bus stop for picking and alighting of the passengers after getting signal from the conductor, he move forward to proceed on the said journey, at that time two wheeler driven by its rider driving the said scooter rashly and negligently without observing traffic rules and regulations coming from behind tried to over take the slow moving bus as there was divider in center of road and as there was no space to pass through the left side of the scooter came in contact with right side front portion of the slow moving bus.
As a result of which the rider of the Scooter lost his balance and fell on the hard surface of road and sustained injuries.
Further the accident and the injuries which had occurred to petitioner is only due to his own negligent act of riding of the scooter.
It is also contention of the respondent that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

Jayamahal Main Road, JC Nagara, Bengaluru, , due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2151 in an actionable negligence?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?

Apart from his evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.B.Ramesh as PW2 and got marked at Ex.P18 & Ex.P19.

10. On the other hand, the driver of the respondent corporation has examined as RW1 and got marked document at Ex.R1 to Ex.R5.
11.
Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.

12. My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3:

 for the following:
 R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-
13.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC bus bearing bearing registration No.KA-57-F-2151, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.
14.
On the other hand, it is the strong contention of the respondent that, the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner.
15. On the basis of the rival contentions of both the parties, it is necessary to rely the evidence placed on record by both the parties.
16. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in- chief by way of affidavit, he has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P7.

Ex.P1-true copy of the F.I.R.
and first information statement, Ex-P2-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P3- spot sketch, Ex.P4- photos of injured, Ex.P5-copy of IMV report, Ex.P6- copy of wound certificate & Ex.P7-copy B- Final Shaik Rafiulla G vs B.M.T.C on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74538220/
3 report.

17. On perusal of Ex.P1, it appears that one Shaik Naveed Ahamed lodged a first information on 23.07.2024 stating that his father sustained injuries in road traffic accident due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
On the basis of first information, the North-East Sub division have registered Cr.No.63/2024 and conducted investigation.
After completion of investigation, the police have filed B- false report as per Ex.P7.
On perusal of Ex.P3-Sketch, it appears that the bus was coming on main road, but petitioner was joining the main road.
Ex.P5 IMV report, discloses that the Scooter bearing No.KA-04-HZ-8076 got damages on scratched mark on head light, indicator, mirror front shape, all round guard.
all rear guard, foot rest break leves and handle.
18. On the other hand, respondent has examined driver of the Bus as RW.1.
RW.1 has placed Ex.R1 to Ex.R5.
Ex.R1 is certified copy of first information statement and FIR, Ex.R2 is Certified copy of charge sheet, Ex.R3 is IMV report of bus bearing No. KA-57-F-2151.
Ex.R4 is certified copy of B-false report filed in Cr. No. 63/2024.
Ex. R5

is certified copy of order sheet pertaining to Cr.No.63/2024 of RT Nagar Traffic P.S.
19.
On perusal of Ex.R1 to Ex.R5, it appears that there were two FIRs registered for same offence.
Cr. No.62/2024 of RT Nagar Traffic PS was registered against the petitioner and charge sheet was also filed against him.
Whereas Cr. No.63/2024 of RT Nagar Traffic P.S. was registered against the driver of respondent vehicle.
The police after investigation filed B-report.
Further, the petitioner has placed Ex.P10 which is certified copy of judgment passed in CC No. 4305/2024 on the file of JMFC (Traffic court-VI) Bengaluru City.
On perusal of Ex.P10 it reveals that the petitioner has been acquitted for the offences punishable U/Sec. 281 and Sec.125 (b) of BNS.
It is well settled principle that the Tribunal has to assess the evidence independently without influence of criminal case.
In this case both petitioner and driver of respondent vehicle have examined themselves.
In cross examination both have denied the negligence on their part.
Both have not adduced any eye witnesses to the accident.

Under such situation, the Tribunal has to rely documentary evidence,
particularly sketch of place of offence and IMV report.
As already discussed above the petitioner was joining the main road as Ex.P3-sketch.
Further, damages were found on two wheeler as per Ex.P5-IMV report.
Apart from these two documents, Ex.R2-certified copy of charge sheet clearly show that accident was taken place due to negligence of petitioner.
Further, the petitioner has not challenged B-final report filed in Cr.No.63/2024 of RT Nagar Traffic P.S.
Ex.R5 is certified copy of order sheet pertaining to Cr. No.63/2024 of RT Nagar Traffic P.S. is clearly shows that B- final report has been accepted.
All these documentary evidences have established that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligence of the petitioner.
If the petitioner could have taken care while joining the main road, the accident would not have taken place.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that petitioner has failed to prove the negligence on the part of driver of bus bearing No. KA-57-F-2151.
Hence, I am answering the Issue No.1, in the Negative.

sentences.text: This issue is with respect to the entitlement of relief claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident, under different heads.

In the light of my detailed discussions held above, I am of the view that, the petitioner herein, has not placed satisfactory evidence on record, to show that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, accident had taken place.
In such a situation, he will not get any compensation.
Consequently, the respondents will not be liable to pay compensation to the petitioner, as prayed for in the case on hand.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 also, in the Negative.

ISSUE NO.3:
21.

In view of my due discussions held above, on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, no order as to costs.
Draw award accordingly.
